run_policy: Focused commands at most five minutes, provisioning ten; no production service, credentials, network, or destructive effect; use disposable directories only.

sources.text: Only the account's owner can grant or revoke; anyone else gets `LedgerError` and nothing changes.
A delegate can view only the accounts that granted them access.
A delegate can never post entries.
Owner, auditor, and teller access is unchanged.
Authorization decisions live in `ledger/auth.py`; callers never compare roles themselves. A refused operation leaves every account unchanged.

premises.premise: can_view(user, 'delegate', account) returns True only when user is in that same account's own delegates set, and the delegates set is per-Account (not shared across accounts) and only mutable through Ledger.grant/Ledger.revoke, which refuse non-owners before mutating.

evidence.text:
if role == "delegate":
        return user in account.delegates
grant/revoke: account = self.get(number); if account.owner != user: raise LedgerError(...); account.delegates.add/discard(delegate)

premises.premise: Adding 'delegate' to ROLES and the new branch in can_view leaves owner, auditor, teller, and unknown-role results of can_view unchanged from base, and can_post still returns True only for role 'teller', so a delegate can never post.

evidence.text: ROLES = ("owner", "delegate", "auditor", "teller"); can_view: role not in ROLES -> False; auditor/teller -> True; delegate -> user in account.delegates; else account.owner == user; can_post: return role == "teller"
